title: Geometric sufficient criterion for all weakly etale covers to split
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring such that $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is w-local [def-weil-pbc-w-local], the quotient space $\pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}R)$ of connected components is extremally disconnected (the closure of every open subset is open), and $R_{\mathfrak m}$ is strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$. Then for every commutative ring $B$ and every faithfully flat weakly etale ring map $f:R\to B$ [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], there is a ring map $r:B\to R$ satisfying $r\circ f=\mathrm{id}_R$.

proof.text: Package the w-locality and strictly henselian maximal-localization hypotheses as IsWStrictlyLocalRing and then the extremal-disconnectedness hypothesis as IsWContractibleRing. These classes contain exactly the stated hypotheses.

In a common ring universe apply the existing existential weakly-etale refinement theorem to f, obtaining g : B to E with g faithfully flat and (g comp f) ind-etale. The composite is faithfully flat because faithfully flatness composes. Apply the existing w-contractible ind-etale splitting theorem to obtain s : E to R with s comp (g comp f) = id. Then s comp g retracts f by ring-homomorphism associativity.

For independent universes, lift R and B to ULift in their common maximum universe. A ring equivalence preserves w-locality by its surjectivity, identifies maximal ideals and their localizations, and induces a homeomorphism on connected components; hence it preserves the class just constructed. Weak etaleness of the lifted map is Algebra.WeaklyEtale.ulift_iff. Its flatness is RingHom.Flat.ulift_iff; its spectrum map is surjective by transporting the surjectivity of Spec f across the two spectrum homeomorphisms. Thus it is faithfully flat. Apply the preceding common-universe proof and conjugate the retraction by ULift.ringEquiv. Evaluation at ULift.up x and application of ULift.down prove the required equality. The transport arguments are fully proved private helpers in the item, introduce no assumptions and include zero rings.
